acceptance: The test asserts ordering or uses an injected clock and contains no wall-clock threshold.
It passes 200 consecutive runs under `pytest -p no:randomly --count` (or an equivalent loop) with 4 CPU-stress workers running.
description:
## Problem
tests/unit/.../test_spark_coverage.py::test_cache_clearing_is_outside_the_timed_window failed on develop after #4529 with 0.355 s against a 0.2 s limit and passed on rerun (`gh run rerun 45705052564 --failed`). A wall-clock threshold in a unit test fails on a slow runner.

## Change
Replace the absolute threshold with a structural assertion (cache clearing is called outside the timed region, using a fake clock or call ordering).

## Decision gates
- Do not raise the threshold or mark the test flaky as the fix.

## Guardrails
- BenchBox work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, make agent-write-preflight); the primary clone is read-only.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run; never bypass or signal the lock, and never kill processes by name pattern (pkill -f); stop only PIDs you started.
- Commits as the configured human identity; no agent attribution.
- No carried or own reimplementation of upstream code without the owner decision recorded in datagen-decision-upstream-gap-policy.
- A choice between a small and a large implementation path goes to the owner with sizes before work starts.
- Report only results that were observed; name anything not run.
